title: Cisco Meraki Splunk TA 3.5.0 static evidence
method: Static source and configuration inspection only; no package scripts, tests, or live API calls were run.

supported_scenario.claim: The dedicated Access Points input collects the network event feed for wireless product-type networks, without a configured event-type filter. It can therefore carry association-family events returned by the Dashboard API, subject to event retention, account access, and optional properties in each response.

source_contract.source: Input stanza name with '://' replaced by '::'.
source_contract.host: Event deviceName/deviceSerial when present; otherwise organization Dashboard hostname; normalized lowercase.
source_contract.organization_context: organizationId is added only when missing; networkId remains whatever the API event supplied.
source_contract.time: occurredAt is retained in raw JSON and props.conf uses it as the timestamp prefix in UTC fractional-second format.
source_contract.serialization: The API event dictionary is JSON-serialized as received, with organizationId setdefault; no association-specific field remapping occurs.

supported_scenario.collection: The TA maps meraki:accesspoints to productType=wireless; calls getNetworkEvents once per organization network containing wireless in productTypes; requests perPage=1000, all pages, direction=next, event_log_end_time=current collection UTC, and startingAfter=max(saved cursor, now minus 30 days). The call does not pass includedEventTypes, excludedEventTypes, clientMac, or clientIp.
supported_scenario.association_visibility: No event-type allowlist exists in the TA collector, so association records returned by the endpoint pass through. The current Cisco Meraki Dashboard API v1.74.0 documentation, dated 2026-09-02, includes an official `getNetworkEvents` example with type `association`, description `802.11 association`, and the fields listed below. Disassociation is not included in this example; no disassociation event is synthesized.

fields.networkId: Expected as API network context when returned; the TA does not add it itself.
fields.organizationId: Added from the configured organization if absent.
fields.occurredAt: Timestamp used for indexed event time by meraki:accesspoints props.
fields.clientMac: Retained if returned by API, but not guaranteed on every event; there is no generic clientMac alias to src_mac.
fields.eventData.client_mac: Retained if returned; src_mac alias is only defined for 8021x_auth, 8021x_eap_success, and 8021x_eap_failure, not association events.
fields.eventData.client_ip: Retained if returned; src_ip alias is only defined for 8021x_eap_success and 8021x_eap_failure, not association events.
fields.deviceSerial: Retained if returned; can be selected for host fallback.
fields.ssidNumber: Retained if returned as raw JSON; no TA alias or validation guarantees it for each event.

limits_and_failure_behavior.initial_cursor: If no checkpoint exists and no start_from_days_ago is configured, the generic collector initializes start_time to one day before collection. The network-events query additionally clamps startingAfter to no earlier than 30 days before now.
limits_and_failure_behavior.checkpoint: Access Points is not a NOT_TS sourcetype or INCLUDE_TS sourcetype. It uses current collection time as its checkpoint and advances it after full stream consumption; checkpoint is not based on latest event occurredAt.
limits_and_failure_behavior.duplicates: If a stream fails after emitting some events, the final checkpoint update is skipped; the next run can repeat already written events from the prior cursor. Deduplication is not performed by this collector.
limits_and_failure_behavior.late_events: A successfully completed run advances the cursor to collection time, without an event-time overlap. A late-arriving event with occurredAt before that cursor may not be fetched in a later run; the 30-day lower bound only caps old cursors, it does not create a replay overlap.
limits_and_failure_behavior.pagination: The packaged SDK uses the Dashboard API pagination links for total_pages=-1. The TA streams these pages. A pagination/API exception after partial writes fails the run and prevents the final checkpoint update; partial records cannot be rolled back.
limits_and_failure_behavior.api_errors: Network-event API exceptions are logged and raised as collector errors; OAuth may refresh once and retry that network. The organization request limiter is shared across TA worker processes and honors the configured max_api_calls_per_second. Other API failures can fail the input; no event is synthesized on failure.
limits_and_failure_behavior.input_interval_issue: default/inputs.conf sets cisco_meraki_accesspoints interval=86400, while accesspoints input validation uses range(360,86400), which excludes 86400. Treat the packaged default as a concrete configuration defect/gate; choose a permitted interval below 86400 and verify via actual TA input validation before qualification.

inventory_and_topology.device_inventory: Dedicated cisco_meraki_devices input calls getOrganizationDevices with total_pages=-1 and emits meraki:devices; props marks this as a snapshot with DATETIME_CONFIG=NONE. It is current inventory, not client association history.
inventory_and_topology.organization_networks: Dedicated cisco_meraki_organization_networks input calls getOrganizationNetworks and emits meraki:organizationsnetworks; this sourcetype is also a DATETIME_CONFIG=NONE snapshot.
inventory_and_topology.lldp_cdp_topology: The packaged Custom API catalog includes getOrganizationSwitchPortsTopologyDiscoveryByDevice at /organizations/{organizationId}/switch/ports/topology/discovery/byDevice. Its catalog summary explicitly says most recently seen LLDP/CDP discovery/topology per switch port; it is paginated and allows t0/timespan, but is not a dedicated input and is not historical association data.
inventory_and_topology.custom_api_contract: The generic custom input can collect cataloged organization GET endpoints and emits meraki:custom, decorating each API item with organizationId, endpoint_name, endpoint_path, operation_id, and collection_time. meraki:custom uses DATETIME_CONFIG=NONE, so event time is ingestion/snapshot time unless searches explicitly parse a retained payload timestamp. The endpoint must be selected/configured; mere catalog presence does not mean it is being collected.

requirements_and_gates.account: A configured Meraki organization account is required; the TA supports API key or OAuth2 auth configuration. The endpoint must be permitted for the organization and the API credential must have access to that org/network's read endpoint.
requirements_and_gates.deployment: The Access Points input requires its modular input to be configured for the organization and an index; the input scheme's only user-defined argument is name. TA default configuration declares Python 3.13. Check the installed Splunk/Python runtime and TA deployment placement for the actual target before enabling collection.
requirements_and_gates.permissions: Static package source does not establish the tenant's effective API role, licensing entitlement, or event retention. These remain environment gates; the Custom API save flow performs a bounded endpoint availability probe, but Access Points validation does not prove association event availability.
requirements_and_gates.archive_gate: This ledger establishes source behavior only. It does not prove that the selected org returns association records, that optional client IP/MAC/SSID fields are populated, or that SHC/Cloud deployment and checkpoint persistence are qualified.

synthetic_raw_contract.safe_fixture_rule: Use only a captured or official-schema-backed response shape, with unique documentation-only identifiers and a fixed UTC occurredAt. Include optional client/AP/SSID fields only when present in the captured/schema-backed example. Do not synthesize client IP, association state, DHCP/NAT state, AP serial, SSID, or event end time from assumptions.
synthetic_raw_contract.allowed_ta_envelope: For a TA serialization unit fixture, the confirmed outer event envelope is one JSON object with API-returned event keys plus organizationId if absent. Do not add TA-invented start/end time or client fields.
synthetic_raw_contract.unresolved_shape: The archive contains no dedicated Access Points sample fixture or event-type catalog. The current official API reference supplies an association example suitable for a synthetic shape. It does not supply an evidenced disassociation example/type in that operation example, so no disassociation fixture is authorized by this evidence.

official_primary_sources_verified_2026_1.document: Get Network Events - Meraki Dashboard API v1 (API v1.74.0, dated 2026-09-02)
official_primary_sources_verified_2026_1.supports: Current operation schema and example: occurredAt UTC ISO8601; networkId; type=association; clientMac; deviceSerial/deviceName only shown if device is an AP; ssidNumber; eventData.client_mac and eventData.client_ip. This is the example's field availability, not a guarantee that all real events contain every optional property.

official_primary_sources_verified_2026_1.document: Get Organization Devices - Meraki Dashboard API v1 (API v1.74.0, dated 2026-09-02)
official_primary_sources_verified_2026_1.supports: Current device inventory schema/example including name, serial, model, mac, networkId, productType and lanIp; paginated endpoint.

official_primary_sources_verified_2026_1.document: Get Organization Switch Ports Topology Discovery By Device - Meraki Dashboard API v1 (API v1.74.0, dated 2026-09-02)
official_primary_sources_verified_2026_1.supports: Current paginated API schema/example: switch item name/serial/mac/network/model, portId, lastUpdatedAt, and LLDP/CDP name/value TLVs; API summary says most-recently-seen discovery per switch port. This endpoint is listed in the TA's Custom API catalog, but custom input configuration and tenant permission are still required.

evidence.supports: Access Points sourcetype, input scheme, only name argument, and interval validation range.
Access Points default Python runtime requirement and interval 86400.
Wireless product mapping, default/30-day cursor handling, exact getNetworkEvents call, network-product filter, OAuth retry and error behavior.
Packaged SDK's documented getNetworkEvents filter semantics, pagination and supported parameters; TA call omits event/client filters.
Host fallback, organizationId enrichment, raw event processing, streaming checkpoint updates after completion.
Sourcetype constants, snapshot/time-series classification, raw JSON serialization and Splunk metadata.
Access Points occurredAt timestamp parsing and JSON KV mode; narrow aliases; device/custom snapshot ingest-time behavior.
Organization network and device inventory APIs / sourcetype dispatch.
Cataloged getOrganizationDevices and LLDP/CDP topology endpoint path, summary, pagination, and parameters.
Custom API input sourcetype and catalog/availability validation.
Custom input poll bounds/limits, metadata decoration, pagination and collection limits.
Catalog-constrained read-only endpoint selection, 3600–86400-second interval, pagination controls, verification probe, duplicate and partial-page replay behavior.
